history.summary: CSV ERROR / DUPLICATE FLAG: this row ('Shri Devi Talab Mandir', Patiala) appears to be a duplicate or misattribution of seq 819 (Shri Devi Talab Mandir, Jalandhar) — see 819.json. Web research finds the famous Shri Devi Talab Mandir only at Jalandhar on Tanda Road (Wikipedia 'Devi Talab Mandir', devitalabmandir.com, Expedia); no Shri Devi Talab Mandir exists in Patiala city. The only Patiala-district listing found is a small, permanently-closed 'Devi Talab Mandir' on Main Road, Samana (30.156321, 76.204089), ~28 km from Patiala — a different, minor shrine. Recommend merging this row with seq 819 or removing it; do not treat it as a second temple. CSV town corrected from Patiala to Jalandhar; district corrected from Patiala to Jalandhar. The actual Shri Devi Talab Mandir on Tanda Road is one of Jalandhar's premier Hindu temples and a 51-Shakti-Peetha shrine to Mata Tripurmalini. Its focal point is a large talab (sacred tank) ringed by a broad causeway where worshippers meditate; in the centre stands a seated Lord Shiva statue from which water spouts like a fountain. The complex includes the main Mata Tripurmalini shrine, an adjacent Kali monument, a large replica of the Amarnath Cave (entered via a footpath lined with tiger statues, housing a Shiva lingam, figurines and paintings), and a mock mountain decorated with giant-sized gods, lions and tigers including a lion's head visitors can step into. A Panjab University academic paper counts Devi Talab among the 51 Shakti Pithas. In December the temple hosts the Harballabh Sangeet Sammelan classical music festival. The Shri Devi Talab Mandir Charitable Hospital stands on Mandir Marg nearby.

name: Shri Devi Talab Mandir
town_description: Jalandhar is one of Punjab's oldest cities, with roots in the Indus Valley Civilization period, historically linked to the Nath tradition and the Shakta cult. The Devi Talab Mandir on Tanda Road, about 1 km from the railway station, is the city's most famous Shakti shrine.

travel.airport: Sri Guru Ram Das Ji International Airport, Amritsar (~80 km); Adampur domestic airport is closer (~25 km, limited service — verify).
travel.railway: Jalandhar City Junction on the Delhi-Amritsar line, about 1 km from the temple.
travel.road: On NH-44; well connected to Amritsar (80 km), Ludhiana (60 km) and Delhi (375 km). The temple is on Tanda Road, reached by auto/taxi.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for pleasant weather; December for the Harballabh Sangeet Sammelan; Navratri for festivals.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Listed as open daily 5:00 AM to 10:00 PM (verify — per devitalabmandir.com listing). Free entry.
